      ggplot2::labs(title = "SVM tuning: mean macro-F1 across shared five-fold CV",
                     x = "Cost (C)", y = "Gamma multiplier (gamma = multiplier / p)", fill = "Macro-F1") +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(14, 18, 14, 14),
        plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13))
    cm <- as.data.frame(result$oof$confusion)
    cm$Within_actual <- cm$Freq / rowSums(result$oof$confusion)[match(cm$Actual, rownames(result$oof$confusion))]
    cm$Text_colour <- ifelse(cm$Within_actual > 0.5, "white", "#17324d")
    p_cm <- ggplot2::ggplot(cm, ggplot2::aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = Within_actual)) +
      ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white") +
      ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%d\n%.1f%%", Freq, 100 * Within_actual), colour = Text_colour), size = 3.5) +
      ggplot2::scale_colour_identity() +
      ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(result$oof$per_class$Class)) +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#eef4f8", high = "#12648a", limits = c(0, 1)) +
      ggplot2::labs(title = "Selected SVM: cross-validation confusion matrix",
                     subtitle = "Out-of-fold predictions; same folds used for tuning",
                     fill = "Row share") + ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(14, 18, 14, 14),
                      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13),
                      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10))
    p_recall <- ggplot2::ggplot(result$oof$per_class, ggplot2::aes(x = Class, y = Recall)) +
      ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#12648a", width = 0.65) +
      ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * Recall)), vjust = -0.4) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.05), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                                 labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%")) +
      ggplot2::labs(title = "Which outcomes does SVM identify?", x = NULL, y = "Out-of-fold recall") +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
    invisible(list(tuning = p_tuning, confusion = p_cm, recall = p_recall))
  }


  result <- svm_run_cv(
    shared$cv_data, shared$cv_folds, shared$x_train, shared$y_train
  )
  result$plots <- svm_plot_results(result)

  # Flat result names match the tables formerly exported as separate CSVs.
  result$baseline_vs_selected <- result$comparison
  result$cv_fold_scores <- result$fold_scores
  result$tuning_summary <- result$tuning
  result$selected_oof_predictions <- result$selected_oof
  result$baseline_oof_predictions <- result$baseline_oof
  result$oof_per_class <- result$oof$per_class
  result$oof_pooled_metrics <- result$oof$summary
  result$oof_confusion_matrix <- as.data.frame.matrix(result$oof$confusion)
  result$best_weighted_cv <- result$best_weighted
  result$weighted_oof_predictions <- result$weighted_oof
  result$svm_training_refit <- result$bundle
  result$split_manifest <- data.frame(
    Animal_ID = c(shared$train_raw$Animal.ID, shared$test_raw$Animal.ID),
    Partition = c(rep("train", nrow(shared$train_raw)),
                  rep("test", nrow(shared$test_raw))),
    Row_in_partition = c(seq_len(nrow(shared$train_raw)),
                         seq_len(nrow(shared$test_raw)))
  )
  result$data_audit <- data.frame(
    Check = c("CSV rows", "Cat/dog rows", "Latest-intake animals",
              "Training rows", "Reserved test rows"),
    Count = c(nrow(shared$data), nrow(shared$data_selected),
              nrow(shared$data_latest), nrow(shared$x_train), nrow(shared$x_test))
  )
  result$metric_definitions <- c(
    "Balanced_Accuracy is mean class recall.",
    "Mean_Macro_F1 is the unweighted mean of five fold macro-F1 scores; SD is their sample standard deviation.",
    "Pooled OOF metrics pool all validation-fold predictions and can differ from fold means.",
    "Selection maximises mean CV macro-F1 across 18 candidates (90 fits).",
    "The same folds are used for tuning and reporting, so selected CV performance is a development estimate.",
    "No test predictors or labels are used for fitting, tuning or selection; the test set is not scored for SVM.",
    "The final SVM and its encoder are refitted on the complete training partition."
  )
  result$session_info <- utils::sessionInfo()
  result
})

XGBoost

We use XGBoost as a non-linear model for the classification. It benchmarks the non-linear predictive signal extractable beyond the linear baseline. We use the same predictor set as the multinomial baseline, one-hot encoded into a numeric design matrix for xgboost. Continuous Age_Years_imputed remains unstandardised, as tree-based partition algorithms are invariant to monotonic scaling (Hastie et al., 2009).

XGBoost is fitted with xgboost::xgb.train, using the five-class multi:softprob objective (Chen & Guestrin, 2016). The predicted class has the largest fitted probability. All configurations use 150 boosting rounds, seed 5003 and no early stopping. Configuration A is the XGBoost model baseline: depth 6, learning rate 0.3 and no class weights; the row/column sampling fractions and minimum child weight retain their defaults of 1.

Show XGBoost encoding, fitting and baseline CV code 
xgb_results <- local({
  # Start from the shared preprocessing RNG state, independently of chunk order.
  if (!is.null(shared$rng_state))
    assign(".Random.seed", shared$rng_state, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(caret)
    library(xgboost)
  })
  x_train <- shared$x_train
  x_test <- shared$x_test
  y_train <- shared$y_train
  y_test <- shared$y_test
  cv_data <- shared$cv_data
  cv_folds <- shared$cv_folds
  model_predictors <- shared$model_predictors
  fold_id <- integer(length(y_train))
  for (k in seq_along(cv_folds)) fold_id[cv_folds[[k]]] <- k
  stopifnot(all(fold_id %in% seq_along(cv_folds)),
            !anyDuplicated(unlist(cv_folds)),
            length(unlist(cv_folds)) == length(y_train))

  # Retain every analysis output in memory for the report tables and checks.
  results <- list()
  keep_result <- function(x, name) {
    results[[sub("\\.csv$", "", name)]] <<- x
    invisible(x)
  }

  outcome_levels <- levels(y_train)
  n_classes <- length(outcome_levels)
  xgb_seed <- 5003L
  xgb_nrounds <- 150L
  stopifnot(n_classes == 5L, identical(levels(y_test), outcome_levels), length(cv_data) == 5L)

  class_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {
    actual <- factor(actual, levels = outcome_levels)
    predicted <- factor(predicted, levels = outcome_levels)
    stopifnot(length(actual) == length(predicted), !anyNA(actual), !anyNA(predicted))
    do.call(rbind, lapply(outcome_levels, function(cl) {
      tp <- sum(actual == cl & predicted == cl)
      fp <- sum(actual != cl & predicted == cl)
      fn <- sum(actual == cl & predicted != cl)
      precision <- if (tp + fp > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else 0
      recall <- if (tp + fn > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else 0
      f1 <- if (precision + recall > 0) 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) else 0
      data.frame(Class = cl, Support = sum(actual == cl), Precision = precision,
                 Recall = recall, F1 = f1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  }
  score_predictions <- function(actual, predicted) {
    pc <- class_metrics(actual, predicted)
    data.frame(Macro_F1 = mean(pc$F1), Balanced_Accuracy = mean(pc$Recall),
               Accuracy = mean(as.character(actual) == as.character(predicted)),
               Weighted_F1 = weighted.mean(pc$F1, pc$Support))
  }
  confusion_table <- function(actual, predicted) {
    tab <- table(Actual = factor(actual, levels = outcome_levels),
                 Predicted = factor(predicted, levels = outcome_levels))
    data.frame(Actual = rownames(tab), as.data.frame.matrix(tab), row.names = NULL,
               check.names = FALSE)
  }

  encode_fold <- function(train, valid) {
    encoder <- caret::dummyVars(~ ., data = train, fullRank = FALSE)
    train_matrix <- as.matrix(predict(encoder, newdata = train))
    valid_matrix <- as.matrix(predict(encoder, newdata = valid))
    storage.mode(train_matrix) <- storage.mode(valid_matrix) <- "double"
    stopifnot(identical(colnames(train_matrix), colnames(valid_matrix)),
              !anyNA(train_matrix), !anyNA(valid_matrix))
    list(train = train_matrix, valid = valid_matrix)
  }

  make_matrices <- function(train_x, train_y, valid_x, valid_y) {
    encoded <- encode_fold(train_x, valid_x)
    counts <- table(train_y)
    class_weights <- length(train_y) / (n_classes * counts)
    weights <- as.numeric(class_weights[as.character(train_y)])
    list(
      unweighted = xgb.DMatrix(encoded$train, label = as.integer(train_y) - 1L),
      weighted = xgb.DMatrix(encoded$train, label = as.integer(train_y) - 1L, weight = weights),
      valid = xgb.DMatrix(encoded$valid, label = as.integer(valid_y) - 1L),
      train_y = train_y, valid_y = valid_y, feature_names = colnames(encoded$train)
    )
  }
  cv_matrices <- lapply(cv_data, function(d) make_matrices(d$x_train, d$y_train, d$x_valid, d$y_valid))

  # In R xgboost 1.x, reshape=TRUE requests an observation-by-class matrix.
  # Recent versions return this matrix directly for multiclass predictions.
  predict_classes <- function(model, dmat, expected_n) {
    p <- if (utils::packageVersion("xgboost") < "3.0.0") {
      predict(model, dmat, reshape = TRUE)
    } else {
      predict(model, dmat)
    }
    if (is.null(dim(p))) p <- matrix(p, ncol = n_classes, byrow = TRUE)
    if (nrow(p) == n_classes && ncol(p) == expected_n && expected_n != n_classes) p <- t(p)
    stopifnot(identical(dim(p), c(as.integer(expected_n), as.integer(n_classes))),
              all(is.finite(p)), all(abs(rowSums(p) - 1) < 1e-5))
    factor(outcome_levels[max.col(p, ties.method = "first")], levels = outcome_levels)
  }
  base_params <- list(booster = "gbtree", objective = "multi:softprob", num_class = n_classes,
                      eval_metric = "mlogloss", seed = xgb_seed, nthread = 2L)

  fit_config <- function(params, weighted, configuration, grid_id = NA_integer_) {
    rows <- vector("list", length(cv_data))
    oof_predictions <- rep(NA_character_, length(y_train))
    for (k in seq_along(cv_data)) {
      m <- cv_matrices[[k]]
      fit <- xgb.train(params = c(base_params, params),
                       data = if (weighted) m$weighted else m$unweighted,
                       nrounds = xgb_nrounds, verbose = 0)
      pred <- predict_classes(fit, m$valid, length(m$valid_y))
      oof_predictions[cv_folds[[k]]] <- as.character(pred)
      rows[[k]] <- cbind(data.frame(Configuration = configuration, Grid_ID = grid_id,
                                    Fold = k, nrounds = xgb_nrounds),
                         score_predictions(m$valid_y, pred))
    }
    stopifnot(!anyNA(oof_predictions))
    list(folds = do.call(rbind, rows), predictions = factor(oof_predictions, levels = outcome_levels))
  }
  summarise_folds <- function(folds) {
    data.frame(Mean_CV_Macro_F1 = mean(folds$Macro_F1), SD_CV_Macro_F1 = sd(folds$Macro_F1),
               Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy = mean(folds$Balanced_Accuracy),
               Mean_CV_Accuracy = mean(folds$Accuracy), Mean_CV_Weighted_F1 = mean(folds$Weighted_F1))
  }

  # A isolates ordinary XGBoost performance; A->B isolates the effect of weighting.
  default_params <- list(max_depth = 6L, eta = 0.3)
  A <- fit_config(default_params, FALSE, "A. Defaults, unweighted")
  message("Completed A: unweighted defaults")
  B <- fit_config(default_params, TRUE, "B. Defaults, balanced weights")
  message("Completed B: weighted defaults")

  tuning_grid <- expand.grid(max_depth = c(4L, 6L), eta = c(0.05, 0.10), subsample = 0.80,
                             colsample_bytree = c(0.70, 0.85), min_child_weight = c(1, 3),
                             KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  grid_fits <- vector("list", nrow(tuning_grid))
  grid_summaries <- vector("list", nrow(tuning_grid))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(tuning_grid))) {
    grid_fits[[i]] <- fit_config(as.list(tuning_grid[i, ]), TRUE,
                                "C. Tuned, balanced weights", i)
    grid_summaries[[i]] <- cbind(data.frame(Grid_ID = i), tuning_grid[i, ],
                                summarise_folds(grid_fits[[i]]$folds))
    message(sprintf("Completed configuration %d/%d", i, nrow(tuning_grid)))
  }
  grid_summary <- do.call(rbind, grid_summaries)
  # The first configuration is retained if mean macro-F1 ties, matching the source analysis.
  best_index <- which.max(grid_summary$Mean_CV_Macro_F1)
  best_params <- as.list(tuning_grid[best_index, ])
  C <- grid_fits[[best_index]]
  configuration_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list(A, B, C), function(x) {
    cbind(data.frame(Configuration = x$folds$Configuration[1L]), summarise_folds(x$folds))
  }))
  keep_result(configuration_summary, "xgb_configuration_summary.csv")
  keep_result(rbind(A$folds, B$folds, C$folds), "xgb_configuration_fold_scores.csv")
  keep_result(do.call(rbind, lapply(grid_fits, `[[`, "folds")), "xgb_grid_fold_scores.csv")
  keep_result(grid_summary, "xgb_grid_summary.csv")
  keep_result(C$folds, "xgb_selected_oof_fold_scores.csv")
  keep_result(data.frame(Training_Row = seq_along(y_train), Actual = as.character(y_train),
                           Predicted = as.character(C$predictions), Fold = fold_id), "xgb_selected_oof_predictions.csv")
  keep_result(class_metrics(y_train, C$predictions), "xgb_oof_per_class.csv")
  keep_result(confusion_table(y_train, C$predictions), "xgb_oof_confusion_matrix.csv")
  selected <- cbind(data.frame(Model = "XGBoost", nrounds = xgb_nrounds, seed = xgb_seed),
                    tuning_grid[best_index, ], summarise_folds(C$folds),
                    score_predictions(y_train, C$predictions))
  keep_result(selected, "xgb_selected_metrics.csv")

  # Majority baseline is selected within each training fold, then scored on its validation fold.
  majority_oof <- rep(NA_character_, length(y_train))
  majority_folds <- lapply(seq_along(cv_data), function(k) {
    d <- cv_data[[k]]
    majority <- names(which.max(table(d$y_train)))
    pred <- rep(majority, length(d$y_valid))
    majority_oof[cv_folds[[k]]] <<- pred
    cbind(data.frame(Fold = k, Majority_Class = majority), score_predictions(d$y_valid, pred))
  })
  majority_folds <- do.call(rbind, majority_folds)
  keep_result(majority_folds, "majority_cv_fold_scores.csv")
  keep_result(cbind(data.frame(Model = "Majority class"), summarise_folds(majority_folds)),
               "majority_cv_summary.csv")
  keep_result(class_metrics(y_train, majority_oof), "majority_oof_per_class.csv")

  # Holdout is scored after hyperparameter selection. It never determines parameters/rounds.
  full <- make_matrices(x_train, y_train, x_test, y_test)
  final_model <- xgb.train(params = c(base_params, best_params), data = full$weighted,
                           nrounds = xgb_nrounds, verbose = 0)
  holdout_pred <- predict_classes(final_model, full$valid, length(y_test))
  keep_result(cbind(data.frame(Model = "XGBoost", nrounds = xgb_nrounds),
                      score_predictions(y_test, holdout_pred)), "xgb_holdout_metrics.csv")
  keep_result(class_metrics(y_test, holdout_pred), "xgb_holdout_per_class.csv")
  keep_result(confusion_table(y_test, holdout_pred), "xgb_holdout_confusion_matrix.csv")
  keep_result(data.frame(Test_Row = seq_along(y_test), Actual = as.character(y_test),
                           Predicted = as.character(holdout_pred)), "xgb_holdout_predictions.csv")
  majority <- names(which.max(table(y_train)))
  keep_result(cbind(data.frame(Model = "Majority class", Majority_Class = majority),
                      score_predictions(y_test, rep(majority, length(y_test)))), "majority_holdout_metrics.csv")
  keep_result(cbind(data.frame(Majority_Class = majority),
                      score_predictions(y_train, rep(majority, length(y_train)))), "majority_training_metrics.csv")

  importance <- xgb.importance(feature_names = full$feature_names, model = final_model)
  importance_by_predictor <- data.frame(
    Predictor = model_predictors,
    Gain = vapply(model_predictors, function(p) {
      sum(importance$Gain[importance$Feature == p | startsWith(importance$Feature, paste0(p, "."))])
    }, numeric(1)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  importance_by_predictor <- importance_by_predictor[order(-importance_by_predictor$Gain), ]
  stopifnot(abs(sum(importance_by_predictor$Gain) - 1) < 1e-5)
  keep_result(importance_by_predictor, "xgb_feature_importance.csv")
  keep_result(as.data.frame(importance), "xgb_encoded_feature_importance.csv")
  keep_result(data.frame(Class = outcome_levels, Training = as.integer(table(y_train)),
                           Holdout = as.integer(table(y_test))), "split_class_counts.csv")

  results$final_model <- final_model
  results$protocol <- c(
    "150 boosting rounds for A/B/C and the final refit; no early stopping.",
    "Seed 5003, two threads, five shared stratified folds; training-only transforms and weights.",
    "Select the highest mean CV macro-F1; ties retain the first grid row.",
    "The existing holdout was examined in previous project versions.",
    paste("R", getRversion(), "; xgboost", utils::packageVersion("xgboost"))
  )
  results
})

Decision tree

A single classification tree is fitted with rpart, using the same eight predictors, training-only preprocessing and five folds. Splits use the default Gini criterion and no class weights. The untuned reference uses the standard complexity settings (cp = 0.01, maxdepth = 30, minsplit = 20) and is evaluated on the same five folds. The complexity grid in Section 6 limits the tree’s depth, minimum split size and complexity parameter. Internal rpart cross-validation is disabled (xval = 0) because the shared outer folds provide the selection scores.

Show complete decision-tree fitting and tuning code 
dt_results <- local({
  # Start from the shared preprocessing RNG state, independently of chunk order.
  if (!is.null(shared$rng_state))
    assign(".Random.seed", shared$rng_state, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rpart))

  # Retain every analysis output in memory for the report tables and checks.
  results <- list()
  keep_result <- function(x, name) {
    results[[sub("\\.csv$", "", name)]] <<- x
    invisible(x)
  }

  classes <- levels(shared$y_train)
  stopifnot(
    identical(classes,
              c("Adoption", "Transfer", "Return", "Euthanasia", "Other")),
    length(shared$cv_data) == 5L,
    nrow(shared$x_train) == length(shared$y_train),
    nrow(shared$x_test) == length(shared$y_test)
  )

  # The saved fold indices must partition training rows exactly once and have
  # the same order as the preprocessed validation labels used by each fit.
  validation_rows <- unlist(shared$cv_folds, use.names = FALSE)
  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(validation_rows),
    !anyDuplicated(validation_rows),
    identical(sort(as.integer(validation_rows)), seq_along(shared$y_train))
  )
  for (k in seq_len(5L)) {
    rows <- shared$cv_folds[[k]]
    fold <- shared$cv_data[[k]]
    stopifnot(
      length(rows) == length(fold$y_valid),
      nrow(fold$x_valid) == length(fold$y_valid),
      nrow(fold$x_train) == length(fold$y_train),
      identical(as.character(fold$y_valid),
                as.character(shared$y_train[rows]))
    )
  }

  # Consistent metric definitions across all models.
  class_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {
    actual <- factor(actual, levels = classes)
    predicted <- factor(predicted, levels = classes)

    stopifnot(
      length(actual) == length(predicted),
      !anyNA(actual),
      !anyNA(predicted)
    )

    cm <- table(actual, predicted)
    tp <- diag(cm)
    support <- rowSums(cm)
    n_predicted <- colSums(cm)

    data.frame(
      Class = classes,
      Support = as.integer(support),
      Precision = ifelse(n_predicted > 0, tp / n_predicted, 0),
      Recall = ifelse(support > 0, tp / support, 0),
      F1 = ifelse(
        support + n_predicted > 0,
        2 * tp / (support + n_predicted),
        0
      ),
      row.names = NULL
    )
  }

  metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {
    pc <- class_metrics(actual, predicted)

    c(
      Macro_F1 = mean(pc$F1),
      Balanced_Accuracy = mean(pc$Recall),
      Accuracy = mean(actual == predicted),
      Weighted_F1 = weighted.mean(pc$F1, pc$Support)
    )
  }

  # Train and predict one classification tree.
  fit_tree <- function(x_train, y_train, x_valid,
                       cp, maxdepth, minsplit) {
    train_df <- as.data.frame(x_train)
    train_df$Outcome.Group <- factor(y_train, levels = classes)

    model <- rpart::rpart(
      Outcome.Group ~ .,
      data = train_df,
      method = "class",
      control = rpart::rpart.control(
        cp = cp,
        maxdepth = maxdepth,
        minsplit = minsplit,
        xval = 0
      ),
      model = TRUE
    )

    valid_df <- as.data.frame(x_valid)

    # Preserve the outcome class order, including classes not predicted.
    predicted <- predict(model, newdata = valid_df, type = "class")
    predicted <- factor(as.character(predicted), levels = classes)

    list(model = model, predicted = predicted)
  }

  # Untuned reference: standard rpart complexity defaults, assessed on the
  # same five folds. Internal CV is disabled because the shared folds are used.
  baseline_config <- data.frame(cp = 0.01, maxdepth = 30L, minsplit = 20L)
  baseline_fold_rows <- vector("list", 5L)
  baseline_oof_predictions <- rep(NA_character_, length(shared$y_train))
  baseline_fold_id <- integer(length(shared$y_train))

  for (k in seq_len(5L)) {
    rows <- shared$cv_folds[[k]]
    fold <- shared$cv_data[[k]]
    fitted <- fit_tree(
      x_train = fold$x_train,
      y_train = fold$y_train,
      x_valid = fold$x_valid,
      cp = baseline_config$cp,
      maxdepth = baseline_config$maxdepth,
      minsplit = baseline_config$minsplit
    )
    m <- metrics(fold$y_valid, fitted$predicted)
    baseline_oof_predictions[rows] <- as.character(fitted$predicted)
    baseline_fold_id[rows] <- k
    baseline_fold_rows[[k]] <- data.frame(
      Fold = k,
      cp = baseline_config$cp,
      maxdepth = baseline_config$maxdepth,
      minsplit = baseline_config$minsplit,
      Macro_F1 = unname(m["Macro_F1"]),
      Balanced_Accuracy = unname(m["Balanced_Accuracy"]),
      Accuracy = unname(m["Accuracy"]),
      Weighted_F1 = unname(m["Weighted_F1"])
    )
  }

  stopifnot(!anyNA(baseline_oof_predictions), all(baseline_fold_id %in% 1:5))
  baseline_fold_scores <- do.call(rbind, baseline_fold_rows)
  baseline_cv_summary <- data.frame(
    Model = "Decision tree (baseline)",
    Mean_CV_Macro_F1 = mean(baseline_fold_scores$Macro_F1),
    SD_CV_Macro_F1 = sd(baseline_fold_scores$Macro_F1),
    Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy = mean(baseline_fold_scores$Balanced_Accuracy),
    Mean_CV_Accuracy = mean(baseline_fold_scores$Accuracy),
    Mean_CV_Weighted_F1 = mean(baseline_fold_scores$Weighted_F1),
    cp = baseline_config$cp,
    maxdepth = baseline_config$maxdepth,
    minsplit = baseline_config$minsplit
  )
  keep_result(baseline_fold_scores, "decision_tree_baseline_fold_scores.csv")
  keep_result(baseline_cv_summary, "decision_tree_baseline_metrics.csv")
  keep_result(
    data.frame(
      Training_Row = seq_along(shared$y_train),
      Actual = as.character(shared$y_train),
      Predicted = baseline_oof_predictions,
      Fold = baseline_fold_id
    ),
    "decision_tree_baseline_oof_predictions.csv"
  )

  # A small, explicit complexity grid.
  # Larger cp values penalise additional splits; maxdepth limits tree depth.
  tree_grid <- expand.grid(
    cp = c(0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02),
    maxdepth = c(3L, 5L, 8L),
    minsplit = c(20L, 50L),
    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Score every candidate on the same five training-only CV folds.
  grid_fold_rows <- list()
  candidate_predictions <- vector("list", nrow(tree_grid))

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(tree_grid))) {
    cfg <- tree_grid[i, ]
    candidate_predictions[[i]] <- vector("list", 5L)

    for (k in seq_len(5L)) {
      fold <- shared$cv_data[[k]]

      fitted <- fit_tree(
        x_train = fold$x_train,
        y_train = fold$y_train,
        x_valid = fold$x_valid,
        cp = cfg$cp,
        maxdepth = cfg$maxdepth,
        minsplit = cfg$minsplit
      )

      candidate_predictions[[i]][[k]] <- fitted$predicted
      fold_metrics <- metrics(fold$y_valid, fitted$predicted)

      grid_fold_rows[[length(grid_fold_rows) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
        Grid_ID = i,
        Fold = k,
        cp = cfg$cp,
        maxdepth = cfg$maxdepth,
        minsplit = cfg$minsplit,
        Macro_F1 = unname(fold_metrics["Macro_F1"]),
        Balanced_Accuracy = unname(fold_metrics["Balanced_Accuracy"]),
        Accuracy = unname(fold_metrics["Accuracy"]),
        Weighted_F1 = unname(fold_metrics["Weighted_F1"])
      )
    }
  }

  grid_fold_scores <- do.call(rbind, grid_fold_rows)

  grid_summary <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(split(grid_fold_scores, grid_fold_scores$Grid_ID), function(z) {
      data.frame(
        Grid_ID = z$Grid_ID[1],
        cp = z$cp[1],
        maxdepth = z$maxdepth[1],
        minsplit = z$minsplit[1],
        Mean_CV_Macro_F1 = mean(z$Macro_F1),
        SD_CV_Macro_F1 = sd(z$Macro_F1),
        Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy = mean(z$Balanced_Accuracy),
        Mean_CV_Accuracy = mean(z$Accuracy),
        Mean_CV_Weighted_F1 = mean(z$Weighted_F1)
      )
    })
  )

  # Deterministic tie-breaking: prefer higher macro-F1, then higher
  # balanced accuracy, then shallower trees, then larger cp.
  grid_summary <- grid_summary[
    order(
      -grid_summary$Mean_CV_Macro_F1,
      -grid_summary$Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy,
      grid_summary$maxdepth,
      -grid_summary$cp,
      grid_summary$minsplit
    ),
  ]

  selected <- grid_summary[1, ]
  selected_grid_id <- selected$Grid_ID

  keep_result(grid_fold_scores, "decision_tree_grid_fold_scores.csv")
  keep_result(grid_summary, "decision_tree_grid_summary.csv")
  keep_result(selected, "decision_tree_selected_config.csv")

  # Save one out-of-fold prediction for each training row, using the
  # selected configuration and the original shared fold assignments.
  oof_predictions <- rep(NA_character_, length(shared$y_train))
  fold_id <- integer(length(shared$y_train))

  for (k in seq_len(5L)) {
    rows <- shared$cv_folds[[k]]
    fold <- shared$cv_data[[k]]
    pred <- candidate_predictions[[selected_grid_id]][[k]]

    stopifnot(length(rows) == length(pred))

    oof_predictions[rows] <- as.character(pred)
    fold_id[rows] <- k
  }

  stopifnot(!anyNA(oof_predictions), all(fold_id %in% 1:5))

  oof <- data.frame(
    Training_Row = seq_along(shared$y_train),
    Actual = as.character(shared$y_train),
    Predicted = oof_predictions,
    Fold = fold_id
  )

  keep_result(oof, "decision_tree_selected_oof_predictions.csv")

  # Pooled out-of-fold performance.
  oof_metrics <- metrics(oof$Actual, oof$Predicted)
  oof_pc <- class_metrics(oof$Actual, oof$Predicted)

  keep_result(
    data.frame(
      Metric = names(oof_metrics),
      Value = as.numeric(oof_metrics)
    ),
    "decision_tree_oof_metrics.csv"
  )
  keep_result(oof_pc, "decision_tree_oof_per_class.csv")

  # Per-fold metrics for the selected configuration.
  selected_fold_scores <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(seq_len(5L), function(k) {
      rows <- oof$Fold == k
      m <- metrics(oof$Actual[rows], oof$Predicted[rows])

      data.frame(
        Fold = k,
        cp = selected$cp,
        maxdepth = selected$maxdepth,
        minsplit = selected$minsplit,
        Macro_F1 = unname(m["Macro_F1"]),
        Balanced_Accuracy = unname(m["Balanced_Accuracy"]),
        Accuracy = unname(m["Accuracy"]),
        Weighted_F1 = unname(m["Weighted_F1"])
      )
    })
  )

  keep_result(
    selected_fold_scores,
    "decision_tree_selected_oof_fold_scores.csv"
  )

  selected_cv_summary <- data.frame(
    Model = "Decision tree",
    Mean_CV_Macro_F1 = mean(selected_fold_scores$Macro_F1),
    SD_CV_Macro_F1 = sd(selected_fold_scores$Macro_F1),
    Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy =
      mean(selected_fold_scores$Balanced_Accuracy),
    Mean_CV_Accuracy = mean(selected_fold_scores$Accuracy),
    Mean_CV_Weighted_F1 = mean(selected_fold_scores$Weighted_F1),
    cp = selected$cp,
    maxdepth = selected$maxdepth,
    minsplit = selected$minsplit
  )

  keep_result(selected_cv_summary, "decision_tree_selected_metrics.csv")

  # Final model: fit on the complete training partition, then score holdout.
  final_fit <- fit_tree(
    x_train = shared$x_train,
    y_train = shared$y_train,
    x_valid = shared$x_test,
    cp = selected$cp,
    maxdepth = selected$maxdepth,
    minsplit = selected$minsplit
  )

  holdout <- data.frame(
    Test_Row = seq_along(shared$y_test),
    Actual = as.character(shared$y_test),
    Predicted = as.character(final_fit$predicted)
  )

  keep_result(holdout, "decision_tree_holdout_predictions.csv")

  holdout_metrics <- metrics(holdout$Actual, holdout$Predicted)
  holdout_pc <- class_metrics(holdout$Actual, holdout$Predicted)

  keep_result(
    data.frame(
      Metric = names(holdout_metrics),
      Value = as.numeric(holdout_metrics)
    ),
    "decision_tree_holdout_metrics.csv"
  )
  keep_result(holdout_pc, "decision_tree_holdout_per_class.csv")

  # Feature importance from the final training-only fit.
  importance <- final_fit$model$variable.importance

  if (is.null(importance) || length(importance) == 0L) {
    importance_df <- data.frame(
      Feature = character(),
      Importance = numeric()
    )
  } else {
    importance_df <- data.frame(
      Feature = names(importance),
      Importance = as.numeric(importance),
      row.names = NULL
    )
    importance_df <- importance_df[
      order(-importance_df$Importance, importance_df$Feature),
    ]
  }

  keep_result(importance_df, "decision_tree_feature_importance.csv")

  message("Decision-tree grid search, OOF evaluation, and holdout evaluation completed.")
  message("Selected configuration: cp=", selected$cp,
          ", maxdepth=", selected$maxdepth,
          ", minsplit=", selected$minsplit)
  message("Mean CV macro-F1: ",
          round(selected_cv_summary$Mean_CV_Macro_F1, 4))
  message("Holdout macro-F1: ",
          round(unname(holdout_metrics["Macro_F1"]), 4))

  results$final_model <- final_fit$model
  results
})

6. Model Improvement

All improvement choices use the shared training folds and mean CV macro-F1. The test partition does not determine weights, feature transformations or hyperparameters in these procedures. The following comparisons show both the improvement attempted and its measured effect.

Multinomial logistic regression

Starting from the M0 baseline, M1 adds inverse-frequency observation weights, wc = n/(5nc), computed from training labels. M2 adds a grouped elastic-net penalty. M3 replaces linear age with a three-degree-of-freedom natural spline of log(1 + age), adds a Dog × standardised log(1 + age) interaction, and includes an age-missing indicator. This allows age relationships to vary across species while controlling unstable coefficients.

For M2 and M3, α ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1} is compared along a path of up to 40 regularisation strengths. The path is generated from the full training partition; fold models estimate preprocessing and coefficients separately. After finding the best α, the largest λ within one standard error of its best mean macro-F1 is retained. The selected logistic model uses α = 0.25, λ ≈ 0.132 when penalised. Grouped shrinkage can remove encoded columns across classes; it does not necessarily remove a whole original categorical variable.

Show logistic regression results-table code 
knitr::kable(lr_cv[match(c("M0 multinom", "M1 multinom + weights", "M2 glmnet + weights", "M3 glmnet + weights + age features"), lr_cv$Model),
                  c("Model", "macro_F1", "balanced_accuracy", "accuracy")],
             digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Specification", "CV macro-F1", "Balanced accuracy", "Accuracy"),
             caption = "Table 1. Logistic model improvement, means over the shared five folds.")
Table 1. Logistic model improvement, means over the shared five folds.
Specification CV macro-F1 Balanced accuracy Accuracy
M0 multinom 0.369 0.386 0.797
M1 multinom + weights 0.430 0.490 0.666
M2 glmnet + weights 0.441 0.499 0.695
M3 glmnet + weights + age features 0.438 0.526 0.630

M3 changes mean macro-F1 from 0.369 to 0.438, and accuracy from 0.797 to 0.630. The selected logistic specification is M2 glmnet + weights. This reflects greater attention to uncommon outcomes rather than a uniform improvement in prediction.

Random forest

We tune the number of trees (num.trees: 100, 300, 500) and the number of predictors considered at each split (mtry: 2, 4, 8). All other settings remain at their defaults. Each combination is evaluated using the shared five-fold cross-validation data, and the combination with the highest mean macro-F1 is selected. Test results are not used to choose the parameters.

Show random forest results-table code 
rf_rows <- rbind(rf_base, rf_selected)
rf_display <- data.frame(
  Configuration = c("Unweighted baseline", "Selected by CV"),
  Trees = rf_rows$num.trees, mtry = rf_rows$mtry,
  `CV macro-F1` = rf_rows$Mean_Macro_F1,
  `Balanced accuracy` = rf_rows$Mean_Balanced_Accuracy,
  Accuracy = rf_rows$Mean_Accuracy, check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(rf_display, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Table 2. Random forest: baseline and selected configuration on the same five folds.")
Table 2. Random forest: baseline and selected configuration on the same five folds.
Configuration Trees mtry CV macro-F1 Balanced accuracy Accuracy
Unweighted baseline 500 2 0.406 0.410 0.809
Selected by CV 300 8 0.465 0.453 0.776

The selected 300-tree, mtry = 8 model increases mean macro-F1 from 0.406 to 0.465. No class weights are used.

Radial-basis support vector machine

A grid compared C in {0.1, 1, 10}, gamma multipliers in {0.25, 1, 4} applied to 1/p, and unweighted versus inverse-frequency-weighted training: 18 configurations and 90 fold fits. Inverse weights were calculated from the current training partition as n / (K * n_class), so their mean per observation was one. We selected the configuration with the highest mean fold macro-F1, breaking ties by lower fold standard deviation and then lower cost and gamma multiplier.

The selected configuration was C = 10, gamma = 4/p, weighting = none. Its mean CV macro-F1 was 0.460, compared with 0.349 for the baseline, a change of +0.111.

  Configuration = c("Unweighted baseline", "Selected by CV", "Best weighted candidate"),
  C = svm_rows$C, Gamma = paste0(svm_rows$Gamma_multiplier, "/p"),
  `CV macro-F1` = svm_rows$Mean_Macro_F1,
  `Balanced accuracy` = svm_rows$Mean_Balanced_Accuracy,
  Accuracy = svm_rows$Mean_Accuracy, check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(svm_display, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Table 3. SVM: baseline, selected model and best weighted alternative on the same five folds.")
Table 3. SVM: baseline, selected model and best weighted alternative on the same five folds.
Configuration C Gamma CV macro-F1 Balanced accuracy Accuracy
Unweighted baseline 1 1/p 0.349 0.377 0.801
Selected by CV 10 4/p 0.460 0.443 0.809
Best weighted candidate 1 4/p 0.453 0.506 0.678

The best inverse-weighted configuration had mean CV macro-F1 0.453, versus 0.460 for the selected model. A small difference in mean macro-F1 does not establish superiority.

XGBoost

For configurations B and C, each training row receives the weight n / (K × nc) (training rows n, classes K = 5, rows in the row’s class nc), passed to xgb.DMatrix. Every class then carries the same total weight, n / K, in the training loss. Weights are computed from the training rows of each fold (and from the full training set for the final model) only.

Four hyperparameters are tuned by grid search: tree depth (max_depth: 4, 6), learning rate (eta: 0.05, 0.10), the fraction of columns sampled per tree (colsample_bytree: 0.70, 0.85) and the minimum child weight (min_child_weight: 1, 3). These control model complexity and the degree of regularisation of the boosted trees (Chen & Guestrin, 2016). For the tuned configurations, the row sampling fraction (subsample) is fixed at 0.80 and the number of boosting rounds at 150. Each of the 16 configurations is evaluated on the five shared folds in cv_data, and the one with the highest mean macro-F1 is selected. To separate the effect of the weights from the effect of tuning, the results below compare three configurations on the same folds: (A) library defaults without weights, (B) library defaults with balanced weights, and (C) the tuned configuration with balanced weights.

Show XGBoost results-table code 
xgb_display <- xgb_cv
xgb_display$Configuration <- c("A. Unweighted model baseline", "B. Baseline + balanced weights", "C. Tuned + balanced weights")
knitr::kable(xgb_display[, c("Configuration", "Mean_CV_Macro_F1", "SD_CV_Macro_F1", "Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy", "Mean_CV_Accuracy")],
             digits = 3, col.names = c("Configuration", "Macro-F1", "Fold SD", "Balanced accuracy", "Accuracy"),
             caption = "Table 4. XGBoost weighting and tuning on identical folds and 150-round budgets.")
Table 4. XGBoost weighting and tuning on identical folds and 150-round budgets.
Configuration Macro-F1 Fold SD Balanced accuracy Accuracy
A. Unweighted model baseline 0.481 0.011 0.461 0.799
B. Baseline + balanced weights 0.464 0.010 0.501 0.695
C. Tuned + balanced weights 0.481 0.008 0.541 0.685

The selected configuration (max_depth = 6, eta = 0.05, colsample_bytree = 0.85, min_child_weight = 1) reached a mean macro-F1 of 0.481 (SD 0.008). Adding balanced weights changed mean macro-F1 from 0.481 (A) to 0.464 (B), and mean accuracy from 0.799 to 0.695. Tuning changed mean macro-F1 from 0.464 (B) to 0.481 (C). Because the selected value is the maximum over 16 candidates, it is the selection criterion and not an independent performance estimate; the held-out result in Section 8 is reported separately.

Decision tree

We compare 24 configurations: cp in {0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02}, maxdepth in {3, 5, 8}, and minsplit in {20, 50}. Selection maximises mean CV macro-F1; ties are resolved by balanced accuracy, shallower depth, larger cp, then smaller minsplit. The selected configuration uses cp = 0.001, maxdepth = 8 and minsplit = 20. It achieves mean CV macro-F1 0.414 (SD 0.011) and accuracy 0.812. The full grid and selected model are calculated in the decision-tree code panel in Section 5.

The untuned reference is evaluated separately from the 24-candidate grid. Table 4a compares its standard complexity settings with the selected configuration using the same fold assignments and training-only preprocessing.

Show decision tree baseline and tuning results

  cp = dt_rows$cp,
  maxdepth = dt_rows$maxdepth,
  minsplit = dt_rows$minsplit,
  `CV macro-F1` = dt_rows$Mean_CV_Macro_F1,
  `Balanced accuracy` = dt_rows$Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy,
  Accuracy = dt_rows$Mean_CV_Accuracy,
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(dt_display, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Table 4a. Decision tree: baseline and selected configuration on the shared five folds.")
Table 4a. Decision tree: baseline and selected configuration on the shared five folds.
Configuration cp maxdepth minsplit CV macro-F1 Balanced accuracy Accuracy
Untuned baseline 0.010 30 20 0.342 0.374 0.800
Selected by CV 0.001 8 20 0.414 0.418 0.812

Tuning changes mean macro-F1 from 0.342 to 0.414 (+0.072), balanced accuracy from 0.374 to 0.418, and accuracy from 0.800 to 0.812. These are model-selection results on reused folds; they do not establish performance on future admissions.

7. Model Evaluation & Selection

Evaluation metrics

For class c, precision = TP/(TP + FP), recall = TP/(TP + FN), and F1 = 2TP/(2TP + FP + FN), using that class’s true positives, false positives and false negatives. Precision and F1 are defined as zero when a class is never predicted. Macro-F1 is the unweighted mean of the five class F1 scores and is the primary selection measure. Balanced accuracy is mean class recall; overall accuracy is secondary. Weighted-F1 weights each class F1 by prevalence and can conceal poor minority-class performance.

Cross-validated comparison

Table 5 reports the mean of the five fold scores and the SD of macro-F1. Figure 5 pools one out-of-fold prediction per training animal for class-specific recall. All models use the same animal assignments, target labels and folds. The folds are also used for tuning, so these are selection results, not unbiased estimates from nested cross-validation. Fold SD describes variation across these folds; it is not a confidence interval.

Show R code

  `Balanced accuracy` = fmt(Balanced_Accuracy), Accuracy = fmt(Accuracy))

Table 5a. Selected decision tree: pooled out-of-fold performance by outcome.
Outcome Animals Precision Recall F1
Adoption 6676 0.852 0.983 0.913
Transfer 3897 0.773 0.859 0.813
Return 1144 0.533 0.236 0.327

Table 5a expands the decision-tree recall bars in Figure 5 to include precision, F1 and the number of animals in each outcome group. These pooled class scores use one validation prediction per training animal; the overall comparison in Table 5 uses the mean of the five fold scores.

XGBoost has the highest mean CV macro-F1 among the five completed models. XGBoost’s mean macro-F1 of 0.481 differs from random forest by +0.015; this small difference is not evidence of a decisive advantage. The practical distinction is its greater recall for Euthanasia and Other. Random forest and SVM achieve about 0.80 accuracy but identify few Euthanasia cases. The selected logistic model has lower macro-F1, although its stronger Return and Other recall makes it informative when missed cases are a priority. The single decision tree has mean macro-F1 0.414; its high accuracy coexists with weak recall for rare outcomes.

XGBoost’s lower accuracy (0.685) is a trade-off: improved attention to rare outcomes comes with more errors among common outcomes. Macro-F1 balances class precision and recall but does not encode a shelter’s actual error costs. Staff would need to determine those costs before adopting a model or decision threshold.

8. Final Results & Conclusion

XGBoost held-out assessment

After CV selection, the chosen XGBoost configuration is refitted on all 12,546 training animals for the same 150 rounds and evaluated on the 3,134 test animals. Test labels do not determine parameters or the number of rounds in this procedure. Earlier project versions had already reported results on this split; this is a reproduced assessment, not a newly blinded test.

Held-out macro-F1 is 0.477, compared with 0.481 in CV and 0.139 for the majority rule. Euthanasia recall is 31.5% and precision is 17.6%: many actual cases are missed, and many predictions of this outcome are false positives. The model therefore cannot determine an individual animal’s care or disposition.

Interpretation and process reflection

Aggregating split gain over one-hot columns identifies Spayed.Neutered (35.2% of total gain) and Age_Years_imputed (32.8%) as the two largest contributors. Gain describes how the fitted trees split this dataset. Correlated predictors can share importance, and these values neither establish causation nor show that a field was available at intake.

Show R code 
predictor_names <- c(Spayed.Neutered = "Spayed/neutered", Age_Years_imputed = "Age at intake",
  Base_Color = "Base colour", primary.breed.group = "Primary breed", has_Name = "Name recorded",
  Sex = "Sex", Type = "Species", has_pattern = "Coat pattern")
importance_table <- data.frame(
  Predictor = unname(predictor_names[xgb_importance$Predictor[1:4]]),
  `Gain share` = pct(xgb_importance$Gain[1:4]),
  `Predictor ` = unname(predictor_names[xgb_importance$Predictor[5:8]]),
  `Gain share ` = pct(xgb_importance$Gain[5:8]), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(importance_table, align = c("l", "r", "l", "r"),
  caption = "Table 8. XGBoost: share of split gain, aggregated across each predictor's encoded columns.")
Table 8. XGBoost: share of split gain, aggregated across each predictor’s encoded columns.
Predictor Gain share Predictor Gain share
Spayed/neutered 35.2% Name recorded 5.3%
Age at intake 32.8% Sex 5.0%
Base colour 8.1% Species 3.4%
Primary breed 7.9% Coat pattern 2.2%

The Data Investigation Process connected the audit to implementation: repeated identifiers led to one record per animal, sparse breeds to training-based grouping, and imbalance to macro-F1 and per-class error analysis. Comparing unweighted, weighted and tuned models showed why a plausible adjustment does not necessarily improve the chosen metric. Shared folds allowed a consistent comparison; a stronger evaluation would fix the complete protocol before examining assessment results and reserve a later period for testing.

Answer to the research question and limitations

Recorded animal characteristics provide useful but incomplete information about shelter outcomes. Among the five completed classifiers, XGBoost has the highest mean CV macro-F1. The tuned weighted XGBoost held-out macro-F1 is 0.477. The close CV scores of XGBoost and random forest, together with their different accuracy and recall profiles, make the choice dependent on the importance of recognising less common outcomes. The results support further evaluation as an aid to staff review, rather than automated outcome decisions.

The largest practical concern is prediction-time availability. In the logistic sensitivity analysis, excluding spay/neuter status reduces mean CV macro-F1 from 0.441 to 0.359; excluding both that field and name reduces it to 0.245. This dependence does not prove leakage, but it makes verification of intake-time values essential. The same sensitivity checks have not been established for XGBoost.

The Other category combines different outcomes, which makes it harder to interpret. The analysis covers each animal’s latest recorded admission at Austin Animal Center. The random test split assesses performance within this dataset; performance on future admissions remains untested. Before operational use at this shelter, future work should verify that predictors are available at admission and evaluate the model on a later cohort. Evaluation at other shelters would be needed only if broader use is intended.

Reproducibility

Show the single-file render command

Show in-memory result verification 
# Recompute evidence from the predictions produced above; this never refits a model.
validation_summary <- local({
  classes <- levels(shared$y_train)
  tolerance <- 1e-8
  checks <- list()
  record <- function(label, condition) {
    if (!isTRUE(condition)) stop("Validation failed: ", label, call. = FALSE)
    checks[[length(checks) + 1L]] <<- data.frame(Check = label, Passed = TRUE)
    invisible(TRUE)
  }
  close <- function(actual, expected, label) {
    actual <- as.numeric(actual); expected <- as.numeric(expected)
    record(label, length(actual) == length(expected) && length(actual) > 0L &&
             all(is.finite(actual)) && all(is.finite(expected)) &&
             all(abs(actual - expected) <= tolerance))
  }
  per_class <- function(actual, predicted) {
    stopifnot(length(actual) == length(predicted), !anyNA(actual), !anyNA(predicted),
              all(as.character(actual) %in% classes),
              all(as.character(predicted) %in% classes))
    cm <- table(factor(actual, levels = classes), factor(predicted, levels = classes))
    tp <- diag(cm); support <- rowSums(cm); predicted_n <- colSums(cm)
    data.frame(Class = classes, Support = as.numeric(support),
               Precision = ifelse(predicted_n > 0, tp / predicted_n, 0),
               Recall = ifelse(support > 0, tp / support, 0),
               F1 = ifelse(support + predicted_n > 0, 2 * tp / (support + predicted_n), 0),
               row.names = NULL)
  }
  metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {
    pc <- per_class(actual, predicted)
    c(Macro_F1 = mean(pc$F1), Balanced_Accuracy = mean(pc$Recall),
      Accuracy = mean(as.character(actual) == as.character(predicted)),
      Weighted_F1 = weighted.mean(pc$F1, pc$Support))
  }
  fold_metrics <- function(oof) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(shared$cv_folds), function(k) {
      z <- oof[oof$Fold == k, ]
      cbind(data.frame(Fold = k), as.data.frame(as.list(metrics(z$Actual, z$Predicted))))
    }))
  }
  check_pc <- function(computed, stored, label, support_name = "Support") {
    record(paste(label, "class labels"), nrow(stored) == length(classes) &&
             !anyDuplicated(stored$Class) && setequal(as.character(stored$Class), classes))
    stored <- stored[match(classes, stored$Class), ]
    for (column in c("Support", "Precision", "Recall", "F1")) {
      expected_column <- if (column == "Support") support_name else column
      close(computed[[column]], stored[[expected_column]], paste(label, column))
    }
  }
  check_folds <- function(computed, stored, label,
                          columns = c(Macro_F1 = "Macro_F1",
                                      Balanced_Accuracy = "Balanced_Accuracy",
                                      Accuracy = "Accuracy")) {
    stored <- stored[order(stored$Fold), ]
    record(paste(label, "five fold IDs"),
           identical(as.integer(stored$Fold), seq_along(shared$cv_folds)))
    for (column in names(columns))
      close(computed[[column]], stored[[columns[[column]]]], paste(label, column))
  }
  check_summary <- function(folds, stored, label,
                            columns = c(Macro_F1 = "Mean_CV_Macro_F1",
                                        Balanced_Accuracy = "Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy",
                                        Accuracy = "Mean_CV_Accuracy"),
                            sd_column = "SD_CV_Macro_F1") {
    record(paste(label, "one summary row"), nrow(stored) == 1L)
    for (column in names(columns))
      close(mean(folds[[column]]), stored[[columns[[column]]]], paste(label, column))
    close(sd(folds$Macro_F1), stored[[sd_column]], paste(label, "macro-F1 SD"))
  }
  check_grid <- function(folds, summary, keys, label,
                         columns = c(Macro_F1 = "Mean_CV_Macro_F1",
                                     Balanced_Accuracy = "Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy",
                                     Accuracy = "Mean_CV_Accuracy"),
                         sd_column = "SD_CV_Macro_F1") {
    record(paste(label, "grid size"), nrow(folds) == 5L * nrow(summary))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(summary))) {
      use <- rep(TRUE, nrow(folds))
      for (key in keys) use <- use & folds[[key]] == summary[[key]][i]
      z <- folds[use, ]
      record(paste(label, "candidate", i, "fold coverage"),
             identical(sort(as.integer(z$Fold)), 1:5))
      for (column in names(columns))
        close(mean(z[[column]]), summary[[columns[[column]]]][i],
              paste(label, "candidate", i, column))
      close(sd(z$Macro_F1), summary[[sd_column]][i],
            paste(label, "candidate", i, "macro-F1 SD"))
    }
  }

  # Every animal belongs to one partition, and every training row to one CV fold.
  record("Training/test animal IDs are disjoint",
         length(intersect(shared$train_raw$Animal.ID, shared$test_raw$Animal.ID)) == 0L)
  record("Training/test animal IDs are unique",
         !anyDuplicated(shared$train_raw$Animal.ID) && !anyDuplicated(shared$test_raw$Animal.ID))
  record("CV covers every training row exactly once",
         identical(sort(as.integer(unlist(shared$cv_folds))), seq_along(shared$y_train)))
  fold_id <- integer(length(shared$y_train))
  for (k in seq_along(shared$cv_folds)) {
    fold_id[shared$cv_folds[[k]]] <- k
    record(paste("Shared validation labels, fold", k),
           identical(as.character(shared$cv_data[[k]]$y_valid),
                     as.character(shared$y_train[shared$cv_folds[[k]]])))
  }
  normalise_oof <- function(x, row, truth, predicted) {
    data.frame(Training_Row = x[[row]], Fold = x$Fold,
               Actual = as.character(x[[truth]]), Predicted = as.character(x[[predicted]]))
  }
  oof <- list(
    Logistic = normalise_oof(lr_results$cv_oof_predictions, "train_row", "truth", "pred"),
    Random_forest = rf_results$rf_selected_oof_predictions,
    SVM = normalise_oof(svm_results$selected_oof_predictions, "Row", "Actual", "Predicted"),
    XGBoost = xgb_results$xgb_selected_oof_predictions,
    Decision_tree = dt_results$decision_tree_selected_oof_predictions
  )
  recomputed_folds <- recomputed_pc <- list()
  for (name in names(oof)) {
    x <- oof[[name]][order(oof[[name]]$Training_Row), ]
    record(paste(name, "OOF training-row order"),
           identical(as.integer(x$Training_Row), seq_along(shared$y_train)))
    record(paste(name, "OOF labels and folds"),
           identical(as.character(x$Actual), as.character(shared$y_train)) &&
             identical(as.integer(x$Fold), fold_id))
    record(paste(name, "OOF valid predictions"), !anyNA(x$Predicted) &&
             all(as.character(x$Predicted) %in% classes))
    oof[[name]] <- x
    recomputed_folds[[name]] <- fold_metrics(x)
    recomputed_pc[[name]] <- per_class(x$Actual, x$Predicted)
  }
  record("Logistic OOF animal IDs", identical(
    as.character(lr_results$cv_oof_predictions$Animal.ID[
      order(lr_results$cv_oof_predictions$train_row)]),
    as.character(shared$train_raw$Animal.ID)))

  # LR uses lower-case names and retains both ordinary and regularised model families.
  lr_name <- lr_results$selected$name
  lr_stored <- lr_results$cv_fold_metrics[lr_results$cv_fold_metrics$Model == lr_name, ]
  lr_columns <- c(Macro_F1 = "macro_F1", Balanced_Accuracy = "balanced_accuracy", Accuracy = "accuracy")
  check_folds(recomputed_folds$Logistic, lr_stored, "Logistic selected CV", lr_columns)
  check_summary(recomputed_folds$Logistic,
                lr_results$cv_model_comparison[lr_results$cv_model_comparison$Model == lr_name, ],
                "Logistic selected summary", lr_columns, "macro_F1_sd")
  lr_candidates <- lr_results$cv_model_comparison[
    lr_results$cv_model_comparison$Model != "Majority class", ]
  close(lr_candidates$macro_F1[lr_candidates$Model == lr_name],
        max(lr_candidates$macro_F1), "Logistic family selection maximises mean CV macro-F1")
  for (model in unique(lr_results$cv_fold_metrics$Model)) {
    z <- lr_results$cv_fold_metrics[lr_results$cv_fold_metrics$Model == model, ]
    z$Macro_F1 <- z$macro_F1; z$Balanced_Accuracy <- z$balanced_accuracy; z$Accuracy <- z$accuracy
    check_summary(z, lr_results$cv_model_comparison[lr_results$cv_model_comparison$Model == model, ],
                  paste("Logistic", model), lr_columns, "macro_F1_sd")
  }
  for (spec in unique(lr_results$glmnet_tuning_grid$spec)) {
    grid <- lr_results$glmnet_tuning_grid[lr_results$glmnet_tuning_grid$spec == spec, ]
    best <- grid[which.max(grid$mean_macro_F1), ]
    eligible <- grid[grid$alpha == best$alpha &
                       grid$mean_macro_F1 >= best$mean_macro_F1 - best$se_macro_F1, ]
    chosen <- eligible[which.max(eligible$lambda), ]
    stored <- lr_results$tuned_hyperparameters[
      lr_results$tuned_hyperparameters$spec == spec &
        lr_results$tuned_hyperparameters$rule == "1-SE (used)", ]
    close(stored$alpha, chosen$alpha, paste("Logistic", spec, "1-SE alpha"))
    close(stored$lambda, chosen$lambda, paste("Logistic", spec, "1-SE lambda"))
  }

  rf_selected <- rf_results$rf_selected_metrics
  rf_folds <- rf_results$rf_cv_fold_scores[
    rf_results$rf_cv_fold_scores$num.trees == rf_selected$num.trees &
      rf_results$rf_cv_fold_scores$mtry == rf_selected$mtry, ]
  check_folds(recomputed_folds$Random_forest, rf_folds, "Random forest selected CV")
  check_pc(recomputed_pc$Random_forest, rf_results$rf_oof_per_class, "Random forest pooled OOF")
  rf_summary_columns <- c(Macro_F1 = "Mean_Macro_F1", Balanced_Accuracy = "Mean_Balanced_Accuracy",
                          Accuracy = "Mean_Accuracy")
  check_grid(rf_results$rf_cv_fold_scores, rf_results$rf_cv_summary,
             c("num.trees", "mtry"), "Random forest", rf_summary_columns, "SD_Macro_F1")
  close(rf_selected$Mean_CV_Macro_F1, max(rf_results$rf_cv_summary$Mean_Macro_F1),
        "Random forest selected grid maximum")
  close(metrics(oof$Random_forest$Actual, oof$Random_forest$Predicted)[1:3],
        unlist(rf_selected[c("Macro_F1_pooled_oof", "Balanced_Accuracy_pooled_oof",
                             "Accuracy_pooled_oof")]), "Random forest pooled summary")

  svm_selected <- svm_results$baseline_vs_selected[
    svm_results$baseline_vs_selected$Model == "SVM selected by CV", ]
  svm_folds <- svm_results$cv_fold_scores[svm_results$cv_fold_scores$Candidate == svm_selected$Candidate, ]
  check_folds(recomputed_folds$SVM, svm_folds, "SVM selected CV")
  check_pc(recomputed_pc$SVM, svm_results$oof_per_class, "SVM pooled OOF")
  check_summary(recomputed_folds$SVM, svm_selected, "SVM selected summary",
                rf_summary_columns, "SD_Macro_F1")
  check_grid(svm_results$cv_fold_scores, svm_results$tuning_summary, "Candidate", "SVM",
             rf_summary_columns, "SD_Macro_F1")
  close(svm_selected$Mean_Macro_F1, max(svm_results$tuning_summary$Mean_Macro_F1),
        "SVM selected grid maximum")
  close(metrics(oof$SVM$Actual, oof$SVM$Predicted)[1:3],
        unlist(svm_results$oof_pooled_metrics[c("Macro_F1", "Balanced_Accuracy", "Accuracy")]),
        "SVM pooled summary")

  four_columns <- c(Macro_F1 = "Macro_F1", Balanced_Accuracy = "Balanced_Accuracy",
                     Accuracy = "Accuracy", Weighted_F1 = "Weighted_F1")
  mean_four <- paste0("Mean_CV_", four_columns)
  names(mean_four) <- names(four_columns)
  for (name in c("XGBoost", "Decision_tree")) {
    result <- if (name == "XGBoost") xgb_results else dt_results
    prefix <- if (name == "XGBoost") "xgb" else "decision_tree"
    check_folds(recomputed_folds[[name]], result[[paste0(prefix, "_selected_oof_fold_scores")]],
                paste(name, "selected CV"), four_columns)
    check_pc(recomputed_pc[[name]], result[[paste0(prefix, "_oof_per_class")]],
             paste(name, "pooled OOF"))
    check_summary(recomputed_folds[[name]], result[[paste0(prefix, "_selected_metrics")]],
                  paste(name, "selected summary"), mean_four)
    check_grid(result[[paste0(prefix, "_grid_fold_scores")]], result[[paste0(prefix, "_grid_summary")]],
               "Grid_ID", name, mean_four)
    close(result[[paste0(prefix, "_selected_metrics")]]$Mean_CV_Macro_F1,
          max(result[[paste0(prefix, "_grid_summary")]]$Mean_CV_Macro_F1),
          paste(name, "selected grid maximum"))
  }
  baseline_oof <- dt_results$decision_tree_baseline_oof_predictions
  baseline_oof <- baseline_oof[order(baseline_oof$Training_Row), ]
  record("Decision tree baseline OOF alignment",
         identical(as.integer(baseline_oof$Training_Row), seq_along(shared$y_train)) &&
           identical(as.character(baseline_oof$Actual), as.character(shared$y_train)) &&
           identical(as.integer(baseline_oof$Fold), fold_id))
  baseline_folds <- fold_metrics(baseline_oof)
  check_folds(baseline_folds, dt_results$decision_tree_baseline_fold_scores,
              "Decision tree baseline CV")
  check_summary(baseline_folds, dt_results$decision_tree_baseline_metrics,
                "Decision tree baseline summary")
  dt_grid <- dt_results$decision_tree_grid_summary
  dt_best <- dt_grid[order(-dt_grid$Mean_CV_Macro_F1, -dt_grid$Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy,
                           dt_grid$maxdepth, -dt_grid$cp, dt_grid$minsplit), ][1, ]
  close(dt_results$decision_tree_selected_config$Grid_ID, dt_best$Grid_ID,
        "Decision tree deterministic tie-breaking")
  dt_pooled <- dt_results$decision_tree_oof_metrics
  close(metrics(oof$Decision_tree$Actual, oof$Decision_tree$Predicted),
        dt_pooled$Value[match(names(four_columns), dt_pooled$Metric)],
        "Decision tree pooled summary")
  close(metrics(oof$XGBoost$Actual, oof$XGBoost$Predicted),
        unlist(xgb_results$xgb_selected_metrics[names(four_columns)]), "XGBoost pooled summary")

  # Held-out predictions are checked separately and never affect selection.
  check_holdout <- function(predictions, label) {
    predictions <- predictions[order(predictions$Test_Row), ]
    record(paste(label, "holdout rows and labels"),
           identical(as.integer(predictions$Test_Row), seq_along(shared$y_test)) &&
             identical(as.character(predictions$Actual), as.character(shared$y_test)))
    metrics(predictions$Actual, predictions$Predicted)
  }
  lr_test <- lr_results$test_predictions
  record("Logistic holdout animal IDs", identical(as.character(lr_test$Animal.ID),
                                                 as.character(shared$test_raw$Animal.ID)))
  lr_holdout <- data.frame(Test_Row = seq_len(nrow(lr_test)), Actual = as.character(lr_test$truth),
                           Predicted = as.character(lr_test$pred))
  lr_test_metric <- check_holdout(lr_holdout, "Logistic")
  lr_test_stored <- lr_results$metrics_summary[grepl("Held-out", lr_results$metrics_summary$Evaluation), ]
  close(lr_test_metric[1:3], unlist(lr_test_stored[unname(lr_columns)]), "Logistic holdout summary")
  check_pc(per_class(lr_holdout$Actual, lr_holdout$Predicted), lr_results$test_per_class,
           "Logistic holdout per class", "n_test")
  for (name in c("XGBoost", "Decision_tree")) {
    result <- if (name == "XGBoost") xgb_results else dt_results
    prefix <- if (name == "XGBoost") "xgb" else "decision_tree"
    predictions <- result[[paste0(prefix, "_holdout_predictions")]]
    m <- check_holdout(predictions, name)
    stored <- result[[paste0(prefix, "_holdout_metrics")]]
    expected <- if (name == "XGBoost") unlist(stored[names(four_columns)]) else
      stored$Value[match(names(four_columns), stored$Metric)]
    close(m, expected, paste(name, "holdout summary"))
    check_pc(per_class(predictions$Actual, predictions$Predicted),
             result[[paste0(prefix, "_holdout_per_class")]], paste(name, "holdout per class"))
  }
  rf_test <- rf_results$rf_baseline_holdout_predictions
  rf_test_metric <- check_holdout(rf_test, "Random forest baseline")
  close(rf_test_metric[1:3], unlist(rf_results$rf_baseline_holdout_metrics[
    c("Macro_F1", "Balanced_Accuracy", "Accuracy")]), "Random forest baseline holdout summary")

  # Majority-class evidence is recomputed directly from training labels.
  majority_prediction <- rep(NA_character_, length(shared$y_train))
  for (k in seq_along(shared$cv_folds))
    majority_prediction[shared$cv_folds[[k]]] <- names(which.max(table(shared$cv_data[[k]]$y_train)))
  majority_oof <- data.frame(Actual = as.character(shared$y_train),
                             Predicted = majority_prediction, Fold = fold_id)
  majority_folds <- fold_metrics(majority_oof)
  check_folds(majority_folds, xgb_results$majority_cv_fold_scores, "Majority CV", four_columns)
  check_summary(majority_folds, xgb_results$majority_cv_summary, "Majority CV summary", mean_four)
  check_pc(per_class(majority_oof$Actual, majority_oof$Predicted),
           xgb_results$majority_oof_per_class, "Majority pooled OOF")
  majority <- names(which.max(table(shared$y_train)))
  close(metrics(shared$y_test, rep(majority, length(shared$y_test))),
        unlist(xgb_results$majority_holdout_metrics[names(four_columns)]), "Majority holdout")
  close(metrics(shared$y_train, rep(majority, length(shared$y_train))),
        unlist(xgb_results$majority_training_metrics[names(four_columns)]), "Majority training")

  do.call(rbind, checks)
})

pc_metrics <- function(actual, pred) {
  cm <- table(factor(actual, levels = classes), factor(pred, levels = classes))
  support <- rowSums(cm); predicted <- colSums(cm); tp <- diag(cm)
  data.frame(Class = classes, Support = as.integer(support),
             Precision = ifelse(predicted > 0, tp / predicted, 0),
             Recall = tp / support, F1 = 2 * tp / (support + predicted))
}
